hook_text: A clinic notice board, a queue in the sun, ten seconds of attention. Can your poster make someone want a panic button in that time, without lying to them?
clip_script: Audience: older people and their families, three metres away, in sun, maybe reading English second. One message: help is one press away, even when the power is off. One action: ask at the school office. Thumbnails first, six matchboxes. Then a headline fifty millimetres tall, one strong picture, three to five benefits in reader's language, a contact box. Hierarchy, alignment, contrast, a third of the sheet empty. Every claim tested: loud enough for the neighbour, yes; keeps you safe, never. No fear. Two languages. Then the ten-second test with strangers.
visual_style: Whiteboard notice board crowded with notices; one calm poster with a huge headline and a hand on a button; thumbnails shuffle into a layout; claims get ticks or crosses; a stopwatch counts ten seconds.
pacing: Audience and message, elements, layout, honesty, accessibility, test.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sketch six thumbnails for your poster.
